DOI:10.1109/access.2026.3671485.abstract: Predicting ship fuel oil consumption is crucial for optimizing fuel efficiency, reducing operational costs, and minimizing environmental impact. Prior work uses either shallow machine learning (ML) algorithms (e.g., AdaBoost, Bagging, ExtraTrees, Random Forest) or deep neural networks that end with dense layers (e.g., BiLSTMs). However, training shallow ML algorithms yields suboptimal performance, while using dense layers into a deep neural network creates a tradeoff between capacity and practicality. To tackle these limitations, we introduce a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) framework that combines BiLSTM, self-attention and a MoE block, and we study three variants: sparsely-gated MoE, CP<inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\mu $ </tex-math></inline-formula>MoE, and TR<inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\mu $ </tex-math></inline-formula>MoE. In terms of the first approach, we use a sparsely-gated MoE layer, which consists of experts and a gating network. Sparsity and noise are added to the gating network for reducing computational complexity. Next, we utilize two variants of multilinear MoE layers, which are based on factorization approaches, namely Candecomp/PARAFAC (CP) and Tensor Ring decomposition. Experiments on the DataBio fishing-ships dataset (three vessels, one month each) show that our best model (CP<inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\mu $ </tex-math></inline-formula>MoE) consistently improves the coefficient of determination (<inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$R^{2}$ </tex-math></inline-formula>) and reduces root mean squared error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), and mean bias error (MBE), relative to Single-Task Learning (STL) - the same BiLSTM + self-attention backbone but with a standard dense head (no MoE) - and the tree-ensemble baselines (AdaBoost, BaggingRegressor, ExtraTrees, Gradient Boosting, Random Forest) under the same ship-stratified protocol. Ablations confirm the contribution of MoE components. These results indicate that input-conditional experts can better fit diverse operating conditions in multivariate ship sensor time series.

DOI:10.1109/access.2026.3680045.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown outstanding capabilities across complex language tasks, but come with massive computational cost and memory footprint. LLM post-training quantizers such as AWQ, SmoothQuant, and QoQ have demonstrated excellent performance under specific configurations, for example, W4A16 (four-bit weight and sixteen-bit activation) and W8A8 (eight-bit weight and eight-bit activation). However, leveraging these quantizers in a mixed-precision problem is a nontrivial task due to the colossal design space and prolonged inference time in LLMs. To address this problem, this work presents UDP (Up-or-Down Precision), a quantizer-agnostic mixed-precision framework that restricts each layer to a low/high precision pair and selects which layers to promote under deployment-driven memory/latency budgets. UDP uses KLD-guided profiling to seed high-quality candidates and a budget-aware genetic search to optimize the layer promotion set. Across Llama and Mistral models and three PTQ backends (AWQ, SmoothQuant, QoQ), UDP improves WikiText-2 perplexity by up to 0.69 over uniform low-bit baselines at the same low-precision setting and outperforms strong mixed-precision heuristics (FlattenQuant, QFeM, AsymKV) by up to 0.11 under identical budgets. In OmniServe on Llama-2-7B (1024/512 tokens), UDP preserves throughput (<inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\leq 0.5$ </tex-math></inline-formula>% vs. W4A8) while reducing p95 time-to-first-token by <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\approx 60$ </tex-math></inline-formula> ms and using <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\approx 10$ </tex-math></inline-formula>% less GPU memory than W8A8. These results show UDP produces practical mixed-precision policies aligned with real serving constraints.

DOI:10.1109/access.2026.3727158.abstract: Recent Large Language Models (LLMs) have driven an intuitive expectation that automated program repair (APR) can be treated as a direct code-rewriting task. However, practical APR systems require generated candidates to be machine-usable, safely validated, and appropriately ranked. This paper uses an RL-guided repair loop as an instrumented diagnostic environment to separate correct-candidate availability from candidate selection. We evaluate all 40 Python programs in QuixBugs using four code-LLM families, four versioned output-contract conditions, and five fixed random seeds. The resulting 3,200 candidate-generation conditions were evaluated with public tests for plausible correctness and a separately defined 1,200-case augmented oracle for semantic correctness. All 40 programs and all prespecified runs were retained. Correct candidates were available in 173 of 3,200 conditions and for 30 of 40 programs, showing that availability was a necessary upstream constraint under the evaluated conditions. Static greedy selection improved the program-level correct-outcome rate over first selection by 10.0 percentage points (95% CI [0.0, 23.3]; Holm-adjusted $p=.25$ ), while the separate sequential comparison improved by 5.0 points (95% CI [0.0, 12.5]; Holm-adjusted $p=.50$ ); neither effect was statistically established. These conclusions are limited to single-file Python algorithmic repair on QuixBugs and do not establish general superiority of RL, a selector, or an output representation.

DOI:10.1109/access.2026.3727805.abstract: Low-bit quantization enables deep neural network deployment on resource-constrained edge AI platforms, and early-exit networks further reduce inference cost by allowing simple inputs to terminate at intermediate classifiers. However, under extreme low-bit quantization, early-exit models suffer from a largely overlooked failure mode in which the confidence of intermediate classifiers collapses, severely limiting the effectiveness of dynamic exiting. In this work, we propose SAGE, a Shape-Aware Gated Early Exit framework that addresses this limitation through a structurally decoupled semantic prior. A lightweight, full-precision Shape Prediction Module (SPM) extracts geometric superclass information from an intermediate branching point and provides a routing signal that is robust to ternary approximation errors. This signal is reused in two ways: the Gated Exit Classifier (GEC) restores feature discriminability and sharpens the exit posterior by suppressing geometrically inconsistent classes, while the Shape-Modulated Residual Block (SMRB) recalibrates downstream feature channels, propagating shape information to deeper exits with negligible overhead (< 0.02% additional MACs). Across experiments on GTSRB, TT100K, and RESISC45 with four backbones (ResNet-18, ResNet-34, PreActResNet-18, and MobileNetV2), SAGE improves the accuracy–MACs and accuracy–latency Pareto frontiers over the Shallow-Deep Networks (SDN) baseline at comparable or better peak accuracy on architectures with dense residual convolutions. On ResNet-18 with GTSRB, SAGE achieves 93.87% top-1 accuracy at only 34.3% effective MACs, approaching the full static network at approximately one-third of the computational cost. On ResNet-34 with TT100K, SAGE surpasses the maximum SDN accuracy by 1.89 percentage points while delivering a $1.40\times $ CPU speedup. On RESISC45, a remote sensing domain distinct from traffic signs, SAGE achieves a $1.97\times $ CPU speedup on ResNet-18. Gains are limited on depthwise-separable backbones such as MobileNetV2, where reduced cross-channel amplification constrains the modulation mechanism. Semantically decoupled routing therefore offers a promising direction for reliable early-exit inference under aggressive quantization.

DOI:10.1109/acsac67867.2025.00083.abstract: Oblivious RAM (ORAM) is theoretically proven to render memory access patterns of a computation completely uniform, mitigating memory side-channel attacks. However, it is accompanied by orders of magnitude slower memory access latency and, thus, is often impractical in many circumstances. On the other hand, Processing-In-Memory (PIM) has been advancing as a solution to accelerate memory-intensive work-loads and mitigate the memory wall problem. In this paper, we explore the new direction of in-DRAM oblivious RAM with a design named PIM-ORAM. We retrofit the currently available commodity PIM hardware to provide future direction for secure computation on PIM, and design PIM-ORAM. Our design proposes split-data ORAM, a parallelizable in-memory ORAM scheme that takes full advantage of the parallel computing power of the PIM while retaining the original security guarantee of ORAM and dealing with the constraints existing in the commodity PIM. We evaluate PIM-ORAM using the PIM -enabled testbed cloud to provide more realistic numerical values. The evaluation shows that PIM-ORAM alleviates the increase of memory bus usage and ORAM access latency when the ORAM capacity increases.

DOI:10.1109/aeeca65693.2025.00141.abstract: As Artificial Intelligence (AI) applications increasingly penetrate high-dimensional sparse scenarios (e.g., recommendation systems, medical image analysis, financial risk control), traditional dense data training paradigms face core challenges such as dynamic sparsity, resource heterogeneity, privacy constraints, and system synergy. This paper proposes an adaptive optimization system for sparse data training, building a four-in-one technology ecosystem of 'sensing-scheduling-security-compilation' through cross-layer collaboration. Our dual-channel sparse prediction model reduces the error rate of sparse prediction from 34.2% to 8.7%. A programmable sparsity-aware chip supports dynamic routing, increasing ResNet-50 training throughput by 2.1 times at 90% sparsity. Our thermodynamic entropy-driven framework improves GPU memory bandwidth utilization from 58% to 89%. For privacy-performance conflicts, we introduce secure sparse computation primitives based on lattice ciphers, improving encryption efficiency by 17 times at 90% sparsity, while limiting model AUC decrease to 2.7% with ε=0.5 privacy budget. Our Sparse-aware IR and Adaptive Code Generator increase BERT-Large Tensor Core utilization from 26% to 83%. The system has been validated across e-commerce, healthcare, and finance sectors, achieving 5.3× performance improvement at 95% sparsity, supporting China's New Generation AI Development Plan.

DOI:10.1109/africon66545.2025.11533795.abstract: Recent years have seen breakthroughs in large language models (LLMs), such as the GPT and LLaMA family of models that have transformed natural language processing. Despite this, their considerable computational and memory requirements inhibit their deployment in edge and mobile environments. In this paper we introduce a modular quantization pipeline that reduces the memory footprint of LLMs while preserving core performance. We evaluate the basic and advanced quantization techniques, including Absolute Maximum Quantization, Zero-Point Quantization, GPTQ, and NF4, and make use of popular toolkits that include bitsandbytes and AutoGPTQ. Experimental results on representative tasks show that 4- and 8- bit quantized models can be run on commodity GPUs and CPUs with acceptable quality loss. Our experiments demonstrated up to 8x compression, making our pipeline suitable for LLM deployment in both edge and industrial scenarios.

DOI:10.1109/aiia68273.2025.11383684.abstract: Automating Facial Beauty Prediction (FBP) remains a formidable challenge in computer vision due to its inherent subjectivity and complexity. Prevailing methods, including Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Vision Transformers (ViTs), have made significant strides but are hampered by architectural constraints. CNNs possess a limited local receptive field, while ViTs face quadratic scaling costs that impede the efficient processing of long-range spatial dependencies. This paper proposes Mamba-Face, a pioneering framework for FBP built upon the Vision Mamba (Vim) architecture—an emerging paradigm based on State Space Models (SSMs). With its linear-time complexity, Mamba-Face effectively models the global facial configurations crucial to aesthetic assessment, offering a more sophisticated interpretation of visual features. A rigorous evaluation on the FBP5500 benchmark dataset confirms that Mamba-Face sets a new performance benchmark. The model attains a Pearson Correlation (PC) of 0.934, a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.198, and a Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 0.251, yielding substantial improvements over established CNN and ViT approaches. Our findings underscore the capability of SSMs to redefine performance in complex computer vision regression tasks and establish a new, formidable baseline in the FBP domain.

DOI:10.1109/apccas67402.2025.11378307.abstract: Transformer-based speech models offer high accuracy but suffer from heavy computational and memory costs, hindering their deployment on edge devices. This paper presents ECHO, an efficient speech processing accelerator that integrates an Audio-Aware Attention tailored to speech tasks. ECHO's optimized attention comprises (1) Signed Bit Fast Prediction for low-cost identification of TOP-P vertical attention, (2) Sliding Diagonal Attention to capture diagonal patterns, and (3) Selective Vertical Attention for accuracy refinement-all without retraining. The accelerator features a reconfigurable mixed-precision processing element and a sparsity-aware dataflow for energy-efficient execution. ECHO achieves the peak performance of 35.85 TOPS at 180.07 TOPS/W, while reducing computation of attention by up to 83.3% with only 0.21% accuracy loss on wav2vec 2.0 for LibriSpeech. ECHO outperforms prior accelerators in energy efficiency, establishing a strong benchmark for speech transformer inference on edge platforms.

DOI:10.1109/apsipaasc58517.2023.10317473.abstract: This paper describes a data-driven music structure analysis (MSA) method that performs segmentation and clustering of musical sections for a music signal. Since the intra-section homogeneity and inter-section difference are important clues for MSA, most studies on MSA have focused on self-similarity matrices (SSMs) computed from various acoustic features of a music signal. The performance of this approach, however, might be limited because the acoustic features used for computing SSMs are designed manually, and multiple SSMs are often integrated in a heuristic manner. To overcome these limitations, we propose a method that learns latent features useful for MSA with a stack of convolution-augmented multi-head self-attention (CAMHSA) layers that compute and fuse multiple self-attention maps representing multifaceted self-similarity. The estimated features are then clustered into an appropriate number of sections with a Gaussian mixture model (GMM). In the segmentation and clustering tasks, the proposed method outperformed baseline methods based on hand-crafted SSMs. In particular, it achieved state-of-the-art performance on the segmentation task. We found that the internal attention maps represent the section boundaries at the fine and course levels.

DOI:10.1109/apsipaasc65261.2025.11248983.abstract: This study proposes MORTM, a new melody generation model that introduces the Mixture of Experts (MoE) architecture to address the challenges of conventional Transformer-based models in handling a diverse array of musical styles. MoE is a framework in which specialized subnetworks (experts) learn to handle distinct musical aspects. Experimental results demonstrate that MORTM equipped with MoE significantly improved predictive accuracy, reducing the perplexity from 4.92 to 2.04 when compared to the model without MoE. It also enhanced music theoretical consistency, with the usage rate of diatonic notes increasing from $\text{7 6. 3 \%}$ to $\text{8 1. 2 \%}$. Furthermore, qualitative analysis implied that the generated melodies were more natural and showed greater variability in melodic features, with effective use of triplets and rests. Based on these findings, this study is one of the first to demonstrate the effectiveness of MoE in the field of symbolic music generation. We conclude that the MoE architecture significantly enhances the expressive power of the generation model, contributing to both musical consistency and diversity.

DOI:10.1109/ase63991.2025.00084.abstract: Managing complex cloud services requires standard operational documentation, but its sheer volume often hinders cloud engineers from efficient knowledge acquisition. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) can streamline this process by retrieving relevant knowledge and generating concise, referenced answers. However, deploying a reliable RAG-based chatbot for cloud operation remains a challenge. In this experience paper, we analyze the development and deployment of RAG-based chatbots for operational question answering (OpsQA) at a large-scale cloud vendor. Through an empirical study of 2,000 real-world queries across three operational teams, we identify five unique OpsQA intent types (e.g., symptom analysis and terminology explanation) and their corresponding requirements for a satisfactory answer, which differ from general software engineering queries. Our analysis further uncovers six root causes leading to chatbot failures—over half stem from query issues (i.e., incompleteness, out-of-scope, or invalid queries), while others are from retrieval or generation issues. To address these issues, we propose iKnow, an intent-guided RAG-based chatbot that integrates intent detection, query rewriting tailored to each intent, and missing knowledge detection to enhance answer quality. In internal evaluations, iKnow improves average answer accuracy from 65.8% to 81.3% with only a modest increase in latency. iKnow has been deployed for six months at CloudA, supporting thousands of cloud engineers in daily operations. We discuss lessons learned from real-world deployment, providing valuable insights for future research and practical implementations in similar domains.

DOI:10.1109/ase63991.2025.00311.abstract: The distributed deep learning training process within large-scale clusters serves as the foundation of contemporary artificial intelligence. However, its inherent characteristics make it particularly sensitive to stragglers, specifically the presence of slow workers, which can significantly decelerate the entire procedure. Observability tools are essential for identifying stragglers within systems. However, the prevailing system profiling tools are either designed for single-node analysis, lacking visibility across multiple workers, or they recognize stragglers but only deliver high-level symptoms, providing engineers with insufficient insight into the underlying causes.We design Kair, a robust production-standard observability tool. Kair uses an innovative hierarchical approach, transitioning from statistical anomaly detection to causal inference. It employs Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistics for the identification of statistically anomalous workers and implements a causal path tracing algorithm to accurately determine the specific operations, such as computation or communication, that are responsible for the delay. Kair has been evaluated in a production cluster of 2,048 NVIDIA A800 GPUs and demonstrated high effectiveness in detecting latent stragglers at the framework level that are often overlooked by conventional tools. It offers precise suggestions that markedly reduce processing inefficiencies and engineering workload.

DOI:10.1109/asp-dac66049.2026.11420589.abstract: The shift of Large Language Model (LLM) inference to edge devices demands efficient hardware solutions that overcome memory, power, and computational constraints. In-Flash Computing (IFC) using NAND flash provides an energy-efficient alternative but requires robust Error Correction Codes (ECC), severely limiting logic area and power budgets. This paper presents BALANCE, a lightweight ECC codesign strategy tailored for IFC-based LLM accelerators. BALANCE introduces (1) a fine-grained bit-level significance evaluation, (2) a layer-level sensitivity assessment leveraging cosine similarity of residual connections, and (3) a stratified ECC allocation algorithm optimizing flash memory placement. Experimental evaluations on LLaMA3-8B demonstrate that, compared to state-of-the-art solutions Lincoln and AiF, BALANCE reduces ECC overhead, achieving area savings of $275 \times$ and $62 \times$, and power reductions of $899 \times$ and $321 \times$, respectively. This is accomplished while delivering 6% and 5.7% higher code rates and maintaining accuracy degradation within 0.5%. To our knowledge, BALANCE is the first work to systematically integrate LLM error sensitivity with NAND flash physics, enabling a new class of highly efficient and powerful IFC accelerators for the edge.

DOI:10.1109/asp-dac66049.2026.11420669.abstract: Transformer-based large language models (LLMs) have achieved widespread adoption, but their growing model sizes impose substantial computational costs. Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) mechanism alleviates this by sparsely activating a subset of experts for each token. However, it still faces two critical challenges: (1) token rearrangement incurs non-trivial overhead of off-chip data movement, and (2) static execution flow fails to exploit inter-expert token reuse. In this paper, we present MoEA, a specialized accelerator designed to address the inefficiencies in MoE inference. MoEA introduces two key innovations: a Direct Token Access mechanism that leverages a hardware-managed metadata queue to eliminate off-chip token rearrangement, and a Dynamic Expert Scheduler that captures inter-expert token reuse patterns and optimizes expert execution order to maximize token reuse. Evaluations on representative MoE benchmarks show that MoEA reduces off-chip memory access by 12.06% and achieves $259.24 \times, 9.63 \times$ and $1.16 \times$ speedups over CPU, GPU and EdgeMoE accelerator, respectively.

DOI:10.1109/bibm62325.2024.10822866.abstract: Single-cell mosaic integration has revolutionized our understanding of cellular heterogeneity, offering unprecedented resolution into cellular states and contexts. While large language models (LLMs) have achieved success in the analysis of single-cell omics data, their application specifically focused on the integration of mosaic data remains limited. Current computational approaches often fall short in addressing these challenges. They frequently depend on assumptions of data completeness and uniform quality, failing to manage the variability and noise effectively introduced by missing data. Moreover, these models might not efficiently process large, diverse datasets or account for biological heterogeneity and long-ranging dependencies across various data types. To address these shortcomings, we introduce the Single-cell Mosaic Omics Nonlinear Integration and Clustering Analysis (scMonica) framework, which employs a LSTM-transformer hybrid architecture. This innovative model combines the strengths of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, which excel at capturing long-range dependencies within sequential gene expression patterns, with transformers, renowned for their attention mechanisms that handle the complex, non-linear interactions characteristic of multi-layered datasets. By leveraging these complementary strengths, our approach enhances the integration process significantly, allowing for nuanced management of the intrinsic heterogeneity and sparsity of mosaic datasets. Comprehensive evaluations demonstrate the robustness and effectiveness of our approach, offering unparalleled versatility and accuracy in multi-omics data analysis. These advancements underscore scMonica’s potential to drive significant insights in single-cell developmental biology, oncology, and beyond. We discuss the underlying technologies, analyze their applications, and contemplate future directions that promise to extend the boundaries of both research and clinical domains.

DOI:10.1109/bibm66473.2025.11357037.abstract: Accurate glioma grading using noninvasive multiparametric MRI is essential to minimize biopsy risks and guide treatment planning. Current AI-based approaches struggle to prioritize 3D pathological features due to the lack of shape-sensitive multi-dimensional spatial features and exhibit channel redundancy, while multi-scale fusion lacks semantic patch (MRI subregion) relationships. To address these limitations, we propose a Wavelet Multi-Dimensional and Mamba-Guided Semantic Graph Feature Fusion Network (WM-MSGFF-Net) for glioma grading that integrates two innovative modules. First, the WaveletAdaptive Feature Refinement (WAFR) module processes features through the Adaptive Wavelet Multi-Dimensional Collaboration (AWMDC) sub-module, utilizing wavelet-based convolutions to extract joint shape-sensitive spatial features across depth, height, and width dimensions, coupled with adaptive channel attention to capture sparse pathological features. Subsequently, WAFR applies Self-attention to model patch-level dependencies. Second, the Semantic-Aware Multi-Scale Feature Fusion (SAMSFF) module constructs glioma-specific graphs from WAFR and encoderderived patches, using cosine similarity to define edges and leveraging Mamba-enhanced Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) to establish semantic relationships. Experiments on publicly available datasets demonstrate that WM-MSGFF-Net achieves an accuracy of 95.7 % on BraTS2020 and 95.6 % on UCSF-PDGM, outperforming 8 baseline methods. By integrating effective volumetric feature extraction with semantic patch relationships, WM-MSGFF-Net offers a promising approach to noninvasive glioma grading that could support diagnostic decision-making.

DOI:10.1109/bigdata62323.2024.10825581.abstract: We are the first to explore the intricacies of LLM compression techniques in the context of text-to-music generation, focusing on the MusicGen Transformer model. We implement and evaluate multiple compression methods, including pruning techniques and low-rank approximations to the MusicGen architecture. Additionally, we analyze the model’s sensitivity to calibration data and assess the impact of these pruning techniques on different music styles. Our results show that the SparseGPT pruning method is more robust than the Wanda method when using limited calibration music samples. Finally, we delve into transformer interpretability, investigating how specific layers within the MusicGen Transformer influence music style generation. We conclude that existing pruning methods can effectively reduce the MusicGen Transformer’s size, making it feasible for deployment in complex music generation models that require handling long sequences of notes.

DOI:10.1109/bigdata66926.2025.11402115.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have demonstrated remarkable performance on tasks operating on graph-structured data. Some applications require exact online inference, which processes all neighbors rather than sampling a random subset to avoid stochasticity and accuracy degradation, while still meeting tight latency constraints. In this paper, we analyze exact online inference and identify two key challenges: head-of-line blocking caused by heterogeneous request processing times, and highly variable memory usage that complicates cache size optimization for balancing computation and CPU-GPU communication. To reduce the average request latency, we propose GSM, an exact online GNN inference serving system with efficient scheduling and memory management. GSM integrates three main components. The parameter tuner optimizes the tradeoff between computation and CPU-GPU communication overhead by finding near-optimal parameters, such as batch in-degree sum and batch subgraph size, for the target workload. The degree-based scheduler groups requests with similar in-degrees into batches, ensuring each batch's in-degree sum approaches the optimal value and prioritizing batches with shorter processing times. The batch divider partitions a batch subgraph to achieve the optimal subgraph size and improve processing efficiency. Largescale experiments on graphs with billions of edges (Papers 100 M and Friendster) demonstrate that GSM achieves up to 89% lower latency and 71 % higher throughput compared with state-of-theart systems. The implementation of GSM is publicly available.

DOI:10.1109/cai54212.2023.00110.abstract: Emotion detection is a critical component in allowing machines to understand and respond to human emotions. In this paper, we explore the potential of pre-trained transformer-based language models, namely, GPT3.5 and RoBERTa for emotion detection in natural language processing. Specifically, we focus on examining the quality of emotion detection in LLMs and their potential as automatic labeling generators to improve accuracy. We observe that GPT’s generative nature hinders its performance in fine-grained emotion classification, whereas RoBERTa’s fine-tuning abilities and extensive pre-training specifically for emotions enable more accurate predictions within a limited set of emotional labels.

DOI:10.1109/cai68641.2026.11536416.abstract: Telepresence and extended reality (XR) platforms increasingly integrate physiological sensing to infer socio-affective traits and personalize interaction. We test whether resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) alone can predict inter-individual differences in callous affect (SRP-CA; a proxy for reduced affective empathy) in a forensic cohort. Using 32-channel qEEG recorded at 500 Hz during one minute of eyes-open (EO) followed by one minute of eyes-closed (EC), we retain 143 quality-controlled sessions from 72 participants, each paired with a session-level SRP-CA score. We implement an EEG-only, leakage-aware evaluation protocol: splitting is performed at the session level and normalization parameters are fit on training data only. EEG is segmented into overlapping windows of 250–1,000 samples (50% overlap), and a lightweight Transformer encoder regressor is trained per window length; session-level predictions are obtained by averaging window-level outputs. On held-out test sessions, the best performance is achieved with 400-sample windows (MSE = 0.0595, RMSE = 0.244, R2 = 0.652), with consistently positive R2 for 250–500-sample windows. To address the specific risk that EO/EC recordings from the same individual could act as an identity "fingerprint" across splits, we run two control analyses (distance-based template matching and a contrastive Siamese network); EO→EC identity matching remains at or near chance (e.g., N=5: 0.198 vs 0.200; Siamese: 0.256 vs 0.200), suggesting minimal cross-condition identity leakage. Finally, an attention×gradient analysis highlights predominantly frontal and temporal contributions (notably FP2/FP1 and F7/F8, with additional midline Cz/Pz relevance), supporting interpretable empathy-related EEG signatures compatible with XR and telepresence assessment and rehabilitation workflows.

DOI:10.1109/caibda70336.2026.11621574.abstract: AI-based ultra-low-rate speech codecs have advanced rapidly in recent years; however, the absence of standardized evaluation benchmarks has made it difficult to objectively compare competing approaches. This paper presents the first comprehensive, multi-dimensional objective evaluation of five representative AI-based ultra-low-rate speech codecs, namely EnCodec, DAC, LongCat-Audio-Codec, Mimi, and BigCodec, across nine objective metric scores spanning six metric families on a unified Chinese-English speech corpus. The nine metrics cover signal fidelity, perceptual quality, speaker similarity, and composite evaluation dimensions. The experimental results reveal a clear performance hierarchy. BigCodec achieves the highest scores across all nine metrics, outperforming all other codecs with its large-scale single-codebook architecture at a bitrate of merely 1.04 kbps. LongCat ranks second with its semantic-acoustic decoupled architecture at the lowest bitrate of 0.87 kbps, followed by Mimi in the middle tier using a Split-RVQ design. EnCodec and DAC, despite their multi-codebook RVQ structure at 1.5 kbps, yield substantially inferior results. Three overarching insights are derived: model capacity and codebook efficiency are the dominant factors for ultra-low-rate performance, the number of RVQ layers is not a reliable performance predictor, and semantic-acoustic integrated encoders offer a viable architectural paradigm at extremely low bitrates. These findings provide empirical guidance for both researchers and industry practitioners in selecting and designing speech codecs for ultra-low-rate applications.

DOI:10.1109/caibda70336.2026.11621826.abstract: Radix sort is a performance-critical primitive in modern AI and database pipelines, yet its parallel realization on vector AI accelerators is throttled by a cross-bucket exclusive prefix sum that, in the multi-thread branch, runs on a single leader thread and scales linearly with the number of radix buckets. At a bucket count of R = 2048, the prefix-sum block consumes roughly one third of the per-pass time and blocks the remaining threads at a barrier. We present an optimization that replaces the scalar prefix sum with a blocked matrix-multiplication formulation mapped onto the on-chip Vector–Matrix Multiplication (VMM) unit of an Enflame GCU300 AI accelerator. The blocked scheme uses two static 16×16 matrices—a strictly upper-triangular all-ones matrix for intra-block exclusive scan, and an all-ones matrix for carry propagation—loaded once per kernel invocation. We further fuse and eight-way unroll the surrounding cross-thread accumulation and inclusive-to-exclusive broadcast phases. On a 2048-bucket 11-bit radix configuration for 32-bit float32 keys, the combined optimization cuts per-pass prefix-sum cycles from 38.7 K to 21.1 K (−45%) and delivers end-to-end kernel speedups of 1.08×–1.61× on float32 sort workloads from 3 K to 200 K elements, where the prefix sum is a critical-path bottleneck.

DOI:10.1109/camsap66162.2025.11423965.abstract: Principal component analysis (PCA) and probabilistic (P) PCA offer linear models that account for low-dimensional structure of high-dimensional datasets. Deep generative models, on the other hand, such as variational autoencoders (VAEs), can capture nonlinear mappings, but often rely on a simple isotropic prior, which limits their ability to represent complex and clustered manifolds. This work develops a generative latent variable model that integrates a mixture-of-Gaussians (MoG) prior with low-rank constraints in the latent space, where each mixture component defines a local low-dimensional subspace. A critical contribution is that the MoG parameters, including both means and covariances, are learned directly from data. For unsupervised tasks, a sparse router network selects relevant ‘experts’ in the mixture-of-experts setting, thereby promoting disentangled and interpretable latent representations. Experiments on MNIST dataset demonstrate that the novel approach generates higher-quality, more consistent samples than standard VAEs or (P)PCA, and better aligns the latent manifold with the true data geometry. By combining nonlinear generation, low-rank covariance structure, and a sparse routing network, the proposed method reinforces deep generative modeling with principled manifold learning, while bridging the gap between supervised and unsupervised setups.

DOI:10.1109/ccdc69976.2026.11559858.abstract: Accurate wind power forecasting is essential for the stable operation of power grids, yet the inherent intermittency and non-stationarity of wind series pose significant challenges. While Transformer-based models have advanced time series forecasting, they often adopt a monolithic approach, failing to effectively disentangle the distinct characteristics of trend and periodic components. To address this deficiency, we introduce BSformer, an innovative dual-stream framework that adopts a modular approach. The model initially utilizes Multilevel Discrete Wavelet Decomposition to effectively decompose the input sequence into trend and periodic components. These elements are subsequently handled through two dedicated, concurrent streams: the Trend Stream utilizes Variable Correlation Attention to capture long-term, inter-variable dependencies, while the Periodic Stream employs a Frequency Enhanced Block to model periodic patterns in the frequency domain. By fusing insights from these two tailored streams, BSformer generates highly accurate forecasts. Extensive experiments on real-world wind power datasets validate the effectiveness of our specialized dualstream design.

DOI:10.1109/ccgridw69005.2026.00045.abstract: Network traffic classification is a challenging task in network security, aiming to accurately identify traffic behaviour through analysis. Identifying normal and suspicious traffic required modeling network flow data, including traffic, attack, and application classification. Traditional rule-based and shallow learning methods are limited because of increasingly complex and massive network traffic. Currently, the mainstream approach utilizes Transformer models, which have gained widespread adoption due to their strong global modeling capabilities and flexibility. However, Transformer models face challenges in training efficiency and resource consumption when processing long sequences. Due to the quadratic complexity of their selfattention mechanisms, these computational constraints prohibit their implementation in large-scale systems. To address this issue, we introduced a linear-scaling Transformer variant of Mamba and proposed a framework that integrates Mamba and Transformer architectures. This model combines the efficiency of Mamba in extracting local features with the global modeling capabilities of Transformer, achieving improved performance on our primary dataset, TON_IoT. Our model achieved an F1 Score of 0.9214 and an accuracy of 0.9204. In comparison, the Transformer-only baseline achieves 0.8858 F1 Score and 0.8852 accuracy, corresponding to approximately 4.0% gains in both metrics, representing a significant improvement over existing baseline models.

DOI:10.1109/cgo68049.2026.11395198.abstract: Modern tensor compiler frameworks like JAX and PyTorch accelerate numerical programs by compiling or mapping Domain-Specific Language (DSL) code to efficient executables. However, they rely on a fixed set of transformation rules and heuristics, which means they can miss profitable optimization opportunities. This leaves significant optimization potential unused for programs that fall outside these fixed patterns.This paper presents STENSO, a tensor DSL program superoptimizer that discovers such missing rewrites. STENSO’s core is a symbolic program synthesis based search algorithm that systematically explores the space of equivalent programs. By combining symbolic execution and sketch-based program synthesis, it generates equivalent candidate implementations. To make the search computationally tractable, STENSO further integrates a cost model with a branch-and-bound algorithm scheme. This effectively prunes the search space, arriving at optimal solutions in a reasonable time.We evaluate STENSO on over 30 benchmarks. The discovered programs achieve geometric mean speedups of 3.8x over NumPy and 1.6x over state-of-the-art compilers like JAX and PyTorch-Inductor. These results underscore the limitations of heuristic-based compilation and demonstrate STENSO’s effectiveness in finding such optimizations automatically.

DOI:10.1109/cisp-bmei68103.2025.11259179.abstract: Accurate segmentation of medical images is vital for disease diagnosis and treatment planning, particularly in identifying skin lesions. Conventional segmentation networks often struggle with indistinct lesion edges, complex spatial structures, and ineffective integration of features across different scales. To address these issues, this work presents MS-DS3Net, a multi-scale medical image segmentation model constructed on the principle of State Space Models (SSM). The proposed framework introduces two major components: a StructureGuided Fusion Module that strengthens semantic interaction between hierarchical feature layers, and a Boundary-Enhanced Decoding Module that explicitly emphasizes edge cues to refine lesion contours. Evaluated on the ISIC18 skin lesion dataset, MS-DS3Net demonstrates substantial improvements in accuracy and boundary preservation compared with mainstream networks such as UNet and UNet++, achieving metrics exceeding 80 %. These results confirm that incorporating state-space modeling with multi-scale feature learning can effectively enhance segmentation precision and generalization in medical imaging tasks.

DOI:10.1109/codes-isss60120.2024.00006.abstract: Smart phones have revolutionized the availability of computing to the consumer. Recently, smart phones have been aggressively integrating artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities into their devices. The custom designed processors for the latest phones integrate incredibly capable and energy efficient graphics processors (GPUs) and tensor processors (TPUs) to accommodate this emerging AI workload and on-device inference. Unfortunately, smart phones are far from sustainable and have a substantial carbon footprint that continues to be dominated by environmental impacts from their manufacture and far less so by the energy required to power their operation. In this paper we explore the possibility of reversing the trend to increase the dedicated silicon dedicated to emerging application workloads in the phone. Instead we consider how in-memory processing using the DRAM already present in the phone could be used in place of dedicated GPU/TPU devices for AI inference. We explore the potential savings in embodied carbon that could be possible with this tradeoff and provide some analysis of the potential of in-memory computing to compete with these accelerators. While it may not be possible to achieve the same throughput, we suggest that the responsiveness to the user may be sufficient using in-memory computing, while both the embodied and operational carbon footprints could be improved. Our approach can save circa $10-15 \mathrm{~kg} \mathrm{CO}_{2}$.

DOI:10.1109/codit66093.2025.11321507.abstract: In Taiwan, the high rate of accidents between pedestrians and vehicles remains a pressing issue. Pedestrian trajectory prediction poses a significant challenge for autonomous systems, primarily due to the complex dynamics of social interactions. This paper develops a pedestrian trajectory prediction model based on the multimodal switch Transformer with temporal attention mechanism. In addition, the Gating Mechanism is used to select the best trajectory from multimodal candidates, while the correlated sampling module learns true data distributions through sampling, improving accuracy, stability, and robustness for real-world safety applications. The proposed model was evaluated on the TITAN dataset and showed improved performance over previous models, achieving a 10.24% reduction in minimum average distance error (minADE) and a 23.04% reduction in minimum final displacement error (minFDE).

DOI:10.1109/compsac65507.2025.00166.abstract: To promptly identify software defects and prevent defective code changes from being integrated into the repository, Just-In-Time Software Defect Prediction (JIT-SDP) has demonstrated promising research findings. Recent studies have begun to utilize Pre-trained Models (PTMs) for training and prediction, yet these models inherently impose input length limitations, leading to forced truncation of inputs. However, previous work has largely overlooked the impact of forced truncation, even though it may inadvertently discard critical input information, leading to degraded model performance. Moreover, some existing methods fail to maintain consistency in truncation during each model construction process, leading to unexplainable truncations and unstable model performance. In addition, previous datasets suffer from limitations and incompleteness. To this end, we construct a large-scale and comprehensive dataset, MC4Defect. Moreover, we propose JIT-Align, which prioritizes code changes within a commit using a semantic alignment algorithm to make full use of the limited input space of PTMs. To evaluate the feasibility of JIT-Align, we first assess the classification capability of our method by comparing it against four baselines across five datasets. Then, we conduct ablation studies on the proposed semantic alignment framework to validate its effectiveness. Experimental results show that JIT-Align, along with its semantic alignment framework, outperforms all baselines in JIT-SDP tasks, with average F1 score improvements of 3.1%-9.6% and MCC increases of 3.1%-9.7% across all projects, exhibiting higher stability and better interpretability compared to alternative approaches.

DOI:10.1109/conecct62155.2024.10677041.abstract: Von-Neumann architecture has been the popular choice for the processing of instructions for various applications. With the scaling of MOSFETs, the performance of logic gate improves and interconnect delay becomes barrier to latency during instruction execution. Solutions for this are logic in memory (LIM), in-memory computing (IMC). In this paper, 6T and 8T static random access memory (SRAM) cells are used for in memory computing applications. 8T static random access memory cell-based logic offers better noise margin and consumes less energy compared to 6T cell-based logic. While observing logical NOR operation using 6T cell the maximum delay of 37.96ps occurs for the input 10 and power consumption of 40.58µW for the input 00/11. When the same operation had performed with 8T cell the maximum delay of 17.67ps occurs for the input 01/10 and power consumption of 157.4nW. Therefore, 8T SRAM based LIM can provide energy efficient solution.

DOI:10.1109/conit69683.2026.11621401.abstract: The rapid expansion of cloud computing infrastructures and large-scale data engineering systems has significantly increased the complexity of monitoring, managing, and maintaining reliable data pipelines. Traditional monitoring mechanisms frequently rely on predefined thresholds and rule-based approaches that often fail to identify dynamic and evolving anomalies in distributed cloud environments. Recent advancements in Large Language Models (LLMs) have introduced new possibilities for intelligent data observability through contextual understanding, automated reasoning, and adaptive anomaly identification capabilities. LLM-driven observability systems can continuously analyze logs, metadata, schema variations, operational metrics, and pipeline behaviors to identify abnormal patterns and provide intelligent insights regarding system health. Such approaches improve the capability of cloud data engineering platforms to detect failures, minimize downtime, and support proactive maintenance mechanisms. However, challenges involving scalability, computational complexity, interpretability, and security continue to influence practical implementation. This study investigates the integration of Large Language Models within cloud data observability systems for intelligent anomaly detection by examining architectural characteristics, analytical mechanisms, and operational challenges associated with modern cloud environments.

DOI:10.1109/cscwd68734.2026.11581519.abstract: Ship trajectory prediction based on Automatic Identification System (AIS) data is critical for maritime traffic safety, yet real-world AIS observations suffer from sensor noise and transmission-induced data missingness. Existing deep learning methods struggle with robustness: recurrent models accumulate errors over long sequences, while standard Transformer architectures indiscriminately aggregate noisy features, leading to substantial accuracy degradation under data perturbations. This paper proposes GCD-Former, a disturbance-resilient framework integrating Gated Causal Convolution (GCC) for adaptive local denoising with Dilated Self-Attention (DSA) for multi-scale dependency modeling. GCC employs learnable gates to suppress high-frequency noise, while DSA uses hierarchical dilation rates to capture long-range dependencies even in sparse data. Experiments on real-world AIS data demonstrate that GCD-Former achieves superior robustness under combined noise and missing-data conditions, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines and offering a reliable solution for maritime prediction under real-world degradation.

DOI:10.1109/cscwd68734.2026.11582537.abstract: Pixel-level segmentation of structural cracks across diverse materials and environments remains a significant challenge due to the high variability in crack morphology, complex backgrounds, and the limitations of existing methods in efficiently modeling global context and fine details. To address these issues, we propose LFAE-Net, a novel lightweight encoder-decoder network that integrates adaptive frequency-domain learning with multi-strategy state-space modeling for highly accurate crack segmentation. Specifically, we introduce three core components: a High-Efficiency Multi-strategy Scanning module, hereafter referred to as HEMS, that captures long-range dependencies with linear complexity; an Adaptive Frequency-Domain Hybrid module, denoted as AFDH, that enhances crack features and suppresses noise through learnable spectral filtering; and a Frequency-augmented Global-context Head, called FAGHead, that enables semantically coherent multi-scale fusion. Extensive experiments on four public crack datasets, including Crack500, Crack896, Masonry240, and SteelCrack, demonstrate that LFAE-Net achieves competitive and stable performance across all benchmarks, obtaining the highest F1-score of 0.8725 on SteelCrack and maintaining an excellent balance between accuracy and efficiency with only 3.01M parameters and 17.86G FLOPs. The results confirm its strong generalization capability and practical value for real-world structural health monitoring.

DOI:10.1109/cscwd68734.2026.11582642.abstract: Multivariate time series forecasting demands simultaneous modeling of global inter-variate coupling and bursty temporal patterns—two properties that classical statistics and vanilla deep architectures rarely capture together. We present HyTransformer, an encoder-only hybrid Transformer with an adaptive dual stream: variate-wise self-attention models long-range cross-variable structure, while a lightweight temporal convolution branch injects locality. Channel-wise gating fuses both streams, enabling data-dependent emphasis on global or local cues. A variate-as-token embedding, scale-preserving normalization, and a linear projection head keep the design simple yet expressive, and attention/gate maps remain interpretable. Across 12 real-world benchmarks, HyTransformer consistently outperforms strong Transformer, convolutional, and linear baselines, setting new state-of-the-art accuracy with favorable efficiency. Ablations confirm that inverted embedding, temporal convolution, and gated fusion are all necessary, showing that Transformers remain competitive once equipped with explicit variate-centric inductive bias.

DOI:10.1109/cvpr52734.2025.00928.abstract: Existing methods enhance the training of detection transformers by incorporating an auxiliary one-to-many assignment. In this work, we treat the model as a multi-task framework, simultaneously performing one-to-one and one-to-many predictions. We investigate the roles of each component in the transformer decoder across these two training targets, including self-attention, cross-attention, and feedforward network. Our empirical results demonstrate that any independent component in the decoder can effectively learn both targets simultaneously, even when other components are shared. This finding leads us to propose a multi-route training mechanism, featuring a primary route for one-to-one prediction and two auxiliary training routes for one-to-many prediction. We enhance the training mechanism with a novel instructive self-attention that dynamically and flexibly guides object queries for one-to-many prediction. The auxiliary routes are removed during inference, ensuring no impact on model architecture or inference cost. DOI:10.1109/cvprw67362.2025.00109.abstract: Comprehensive exploration of information in complex 4D Light Fields (LF) is crucial for advancing Light Field image Super-Resolution (LFSR). Existing state-of-the-art methods based on CNN or Transformer typically decompose the 4D LF into 2D subspaces, limiting feature learning to specific aspects such as disparity cues or spatialangular correlations. Therefore, they exhibit deficiencies in comprehensive subspace information integration and insufficient cross-domain feature interaction. Moreover, the potential of hybrid architectures that leverage multiple computational paradigms remains largely unexplored in LFSR. To overcome these limitations, we propose LFTramba, a novel hybrid network architecture that facilitates collaborative learning across multiple subspaces through a Transformer-Mamba framework. Specifically, the SpatialAngular Mamba Block (SAMB), built on an efficient visual state space representation, alternates between capturing complementary spatial-angular features in the spatial and angular domains. Concurrently, the Epipolar Plane Transformer Block (EPTB) extracts disparity features alternately from horizontal and vertical Epipolar Plane Image (EPI) domains. Extensive experiments on real and synthetic datasets confirm that LFTramba surpasses existing LFSR methods while maintaining high computational efficiency. Notably, it achieved 3rd in Track 1 and 5th in Track 2 of the NTIRE 2025 Light Field Image Super-Resolution Challenge, highlighting its superior performance.

DOI:10.1109/cvprw67362.2025.00180.abstract: RGB photo enhancement is a common computer vision problem with numerous practical application to mobile cameras and on-device photo processing. This creates a need for solutions that are not only performant but are additionally compatible with real mobile AI hardware such as GPUs or NPUs. In this Mobile AI challenge, we address this problem and propose the participants to design efficient RGB image enhancement models that can demonstrate fast inference times on mobile GPUs. For this, the participants were provided with a large-scale DPED dataset consisting of RGB image pairs captured with an old iPhone 3GS smartphone and a professional Canon 70D DSLR camera. The runtime of all models was evaluated on the latest Adreno and Mali GPUs used in Qualcomm and MediaTek chipsets. The proposed solutions are compatible with all recent mobile GPUs, being able to process HD resolution photos under 65 ms in the majority of cases while delivering high-fidelity results. A comprehensive description of the models developed in the challenge is provided in this paper.

DOI:10.1109/dac63849.2025.11132980.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have transformed numerous AI applications, with on-device deployment becoming increasingly important for reducing cloud computing costs and protecting user privacy. However, the astronomical model size and limited hardware resources pose significant deployment challenges. Model quantization is a promising approach to mitigate this gap, but the presence of outliers in LLMs reduces its effectiveness. Previous efforts addressed this issue by employing compression-based encoding for mixed-precision quantization. These approaches struggle to balance model accuracy with hardware efficiency due to their value-wise outlier granularity and complex encoding/decoding hardware logic. To address this, we propose PISA (Precision-Slice Framework), an acceleration framework that exploits massive sparsity in the higher-order part of LLMs by splitting 16-bit values into a 4-bit/12-bit format. Crucially, PISA introduces an early bird mechanism that leverages the high-order 4-bit computation to predict the importance of the full calculation result. This mechanism enables efficient computational skips by continuing execution only for important computations and using preset values for less significant ones. This scheme can be efficiently integrated with existing hardware accelerators like systolic arrays without complex encoding/decoding. As a result, PISA outperforms state-of-the-art precision-aware accelerators, achieving a $1.3-4.3 \times$ performance boost and $14.3-66.7 \%$ greater energy efficiency, with minimal model accuracy loss. This approach enables more efficient ondevice LLM deployment, effectively balancing computational efficiency and model accuracy.

DOI:10.1109/ectc51846.2026.00146.abstract: The rapid growth of large-scale AI models has exposed fundamental limitations in traditional data center interconnects, particularly in bandwidth, latency, and power efficiency. As compute architectures scale from a few accelerators per server to thousands across multi-rack clusters, copper-based links fail to meet performance requirements. This paper introduces Photonic Fabric™, a silicon photonics-based interconnect platform purpose-built for scale-up AI networks. Photonic Fabric integrates three core technologies: PFLink™, a chiplet/IP optical link supporting UCIe-A interfaces with Gen1 bandwidth of 14.4 Tbps and reach beyond 50 meters; PFSwitch™, a system-in-package switch enabling all-to-all XPU connectivity; and OMIB™, an optical multichip interface for large package integration. Leveraging electro-absorption modulators for thermal stability and advanced 2.5D packaging, Photonic Fabric delivers nanosecond-class latency and ultra-high bandwidth while supporting in-network memory and compute. A 56 Gb/s optical link was validated on a 5nm CMOS test vehicle. Additionally, system-level simulations of a Photonic Fabric-based memory appliance with >32 TB shared memory capacity, 115 Tbps aggregate bandwidth, predict 60–90% communication-related power savings, and up to 5.6× throughput improvement for trillion-parameter models compared to NVIDIA DGX-H100 systems. These results establish Photonic Fabric as a scalable, energy-efficient solution for next-generation AI infrastructure.

DOI:10.1109/eiecc67963.2025.11409632.abstract: With the explosive growth of trillion-parameter large language models, GPU cluster scale-up interconnect technology has emerged as a critical bottleneck limiting the efficiency of distributed training. Its performance optimization and systemlevel innovation directly determine the effective utilization of large-scale computing resources in modern AI workloads. This paper systematically reviews the evolutionary trajectory and industry landscape of scale-up interconnect technologies for AI clusters. Starting from the fundamental technological driving forces, we first analyze the extreme requirements for ultra-low latency and ultra-high bandwidth imposed by the high-frequency, large-volume communication patterns inherent in tensor parallelism (TP). Building on this analysis, we conduct an in-depth comparison of architectural designs and performance trade-offs across different technological routes, including NVIDIA's proprietary solutions and open alternatives such as RDMAintegrated interconnects, memory-semantic Ethernet, and PCIebased fabrics. In addition, the role of scenario-specific innovations is examined through representative examples such as Tesla's System-on-Wafer (SoW) architecture and the TTP/TTPoE protocol stack. Our analysis indicates that AI cluster scale-up interconnect technologies are evolving toward a pattern in which proprietary solutions dominate ultra-large-scale deployments, open standards gain advantages through ecosystem scalability, and optical interconnects progressively overcome physical limitations. Looking forward, performance breakthroughs, convergence toward open standards, and deep integration across heterogeneous technologies are expected to define the core development trends of next-generation interconnect systems. This work provides both theoretical insights and practical guidance for interconnect technology selection in ultra-large-scale AI clusters, as well as for the design of future high-performance interconnect architectures.

DOI:10.1109/eiecs67708.2025.11283488.abstract: Time series forecasting requires modeling long-term trends, periodic patterns, and irregular residuals, which conventional decomposition methods often fail to capture effectively. We propose KMT-Net, a framework that integrates Reversible Instance Normalization (RevIN), multi-component decomposition, a Mamba Encoder, and shared Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KAN). The input series is normalized with RevIN and decomposed into trend, seasonal, and residual components. The residual, containing complex non-periodic fluctuations, is modeled by the Mamba Encoder to capture long-range dependencies. All components are then refined through the shared KAN to capture nonlinear interactions before being recombined into the final forecast. Experiments on the ETT benchmark demonstrate that KMT-Net consistently improves long-term forecasting performance, showing robustness and effectiveness in modeling diverse temporal dynamics compared with state-of-the-art baselines.

DOI:10.1109/eiect68017.2025.11331608.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models enable end-to-end learning from visual inputs to actions for robotic manipulation. Lightweight designs are necessary in resource-constrained scenarios but limit spatial understanding, which can lead to failure in high-precision manipulation tasks. To overcome this challenge, we propose a method that embeds spatial cues into task instructions, allowing lightweight VLAs to acquire richer spatial understanding from task instrcutions. Simulated and realworld experiments show that our method improves grasping success by around 8% and also enhances performance in other manipulation tasks such as stacking. These results demonstrate that instruction-level spatial information augmentation improves task performance while preserving the lightweight nature of models.

DOI:10.1109/eitce70137.2026.11634352.abstract: FlexLLMGen is a representative heterogeneous-memory inference framework, but its original implementation is centered on OPT-style dense decoders and cannot directly run recent Qwen3 dense and mixture-of-experts (MoE) checkpoints. This paper presents a two-stage adaptation of FlexLLMGen to Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen3-30B-A3B. Beyond compatibility itself, the main technical contribution is a scheduler-preserving migration abstraction that separates model-family adaptation into three reusable adapters: configuration translation, checkpoint normalization, and operator replacement, with differential verification as a built-in validation layer. Starting from the original OPT-oriented assumptions in FlexLLMGen, we introduce a Qwen3-specific configuration path, a unified checkpoint-normalization pipeline from Hugging Face safetensors to runtime-consumable numpy weights, and runtime support for RoPE, grouped-query attention, SwiGLU, Q/K normalization, router execution, and shared experts. Experiments cover memory, latency, throughput, sequence-length sensitivity, and a dense output-fidelity proxy under single-GPU heterogeneous offloading. For Qwen3-0.6B, changing from no offloading to CPU/disk-heavy offloading reduces peak GPU memory from 2.039 GB to 1.206 GB, a 40.9% reduction, while end-to-end throughput drops from 9.50 to 5.85 tokens/s at the 64/64 setting. For Qwen3-30B-A3B, the analytical direct-loading baseline is about 60 GB in bf16/fp16 parameter storage, whereas the adapted Flex offloading path completes execution with only 1.716–2.334 GB peak GPU memory, corresponding to about 96.1%–97.1% memory reduction across tested prompt/generation lengths. These results show that the proposed approach makes FlexLLMGen compatible with both Qwen3 dense and Qwen3 MoE models, preserves its offloading-based memory advantage, and offers a reusable migration recipe for other modern dense and sparse decoder families.

DOI:10.1109/eleco69582.2025.11329266.abstract: In this study, a deep learning-based method is proposed that aims to automatically colorize grayscale or black-and-white images. As the basic structure, the SIGGRAPHGenerator architecture, which yields successful results in color transfer, was used, and various improvement modules were added to this architecture. At the initial stage, Dropout, Residual Block, and Batch Normalization layers were integrated into the relevant model. However, upon finding that these modules provided limited benefit, the Instance Normalization approach was preferred as a more effective normalization method, and the CBAM (Convolutional Block Attention Module) module was added to the model as the attention mechanism. In this way, the model capacity to focus on important features in the input image was increased. The model was trained on the COCO 2017 dataset, which contains approximately 117,000 images. The experimental results show that the proposed method achieves significant improvements compared to baseline architecture.

DOI:10.1109/globecom54140.2023.10436793.abstract: Semantic communications have been regarded as a promising solution for the next generation communication systems to alleviate the spectral resource shortage and the network congestion. Existing image semantic communication systems extract and transmit global semantics, which can cope with the downstream data reconstruction or intelligent tasks. However, the semantics involved in these methods are still severely redundant and uninterpretable. In this work, we propose a novel task-oriented semantic communication framework based on scene graph, named DeepSC-SG. Specifically, we first devise a scene graph based semantic encoder, which extracts the explainable scene graph semantics from the input images and encodes the semantics into informative graph embeddings. Then we design a joint source-channel (JSC) codec to combat physical channel impairment. After receiving the semantics, a semantic decoder is devised to achieve the downstream image retrieval task by computing scene graph similarities. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed DeepSC-SG is fairly robust to the channel variations compared to the traditional communication systems, which has great potential in realizing downstream intelligent tasks like image retrieval with significantly reduced size of transmitted data.

DOI:10.1109/honet67928.2025.11318507.abstract: Due to the inherent complexity of mathematical notations, which standard OCR (Optical Character Recognition) technology is not well suited for, retrieving LaTeX code from scans of mathematical equations remains a persistent challenge in document digitization. Using large vision-language models (VLMs), Qwen2-VL and LLaVA-1.5, which are intended to process both visual and text inputs, we investigate a modern, efficient method in this project. To achieve a significant reduction in computation overhead without compromising competitive performance, these models are trained using 4-bit quantization and Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA). Our models are trained to convert equations rendered into accurate LaTeX markup using the LaTeX-OCR dataset as a benchmark. We enable memory-efficient fine-tuning on consumer-class GPUs by utilizing the Unsloth training framework, which enables the solution to be deployed for wider use. In order to have a useful, scalable pipeline for understanding mathematical content in real-world applications, we compare the models using BLEU and ROUGE scores.

DOI:10.1109/hpec67600.2025.11196684.abstract: Recent years have witnessed the prosperity of Sparse Deep Neural Networks (SpDNNs), as they are more parameter-efficient and cost-effective than their dense counterparts. To further reduce costs, it is prevalent for AI companies and research groups to manage GPU servers in a multi-tenant manner that handles multiple inference requests simultaneously. However, SpDNNs suffer from intricate data dependency and low GPU resource utilization, which impedes the efficiency of batched inference. To tackle the above problems, we propose CoSpDNN, which optimizes SpDNNs through exploiting intra-kernel and inter-kernel concurrency on GPUs. On one hand, we design a fine-grained pipeline in inference kernels to minimize bubbles and improve concurrency among GPU resources. On the other hand, we develop an adaptive scheduling strategy to enable efficient spatial sharing of GPUs among multiple inference tasks. We evaluate CoSpDNN through extensive experiments, and the results demonstrate that our work outperforms previous champions in task completion time on a single SpDNN and diverse SpDNNs.

DOI:10.1109/i5cps67958.2026.11452348.abstract: Indian Supreme Court judgments frequently run to 15,000-50,000 tokens—well beyond the context windows of conventional transformers—and any attempt to truncate them risks discarding legally decisive information. Classical self-attention scales quadratically, rendering full-document processing impractical at these lengths. We introduce the Quantum Entanglement-Enhanced Attention Mechanism (QEAM), a hybrid quantum-classical architecture whose complexity grows only as O(n) yet retains O(n2) attention expressivity by exploiting quantum entanglement. At the heart of QEAM lies a Legal-Structure-Informed Entanglement Circuit organised into four hierarchical levels—token, sentence, section, and document—each tailored to the way Indian legal texts are actually structured. Rather than computing every pairwise interaction, the circuit extracts attention weights through quantum interference measurements. On the Indian Legal Documents Corpus (ILDC), QEAM reaches 88.7% judgment-prediction accuracy, a margin of 5.5 percentage points over BigBird (84.1%) and 12.0 over InLegalBERT (79.2%), with a 6× wall-clock speedup once documents exceed 50,000 tokens. Because the entanglement topology mirrors the legal reasoning chain, the resulting attention maps are inherently traceable—an important step toward satisfying Article 21's mandate for reasoned judicial orders.

DOI:10.1109/ic-eeta66496.2025.11548205.abstract: The vast increase in the research articles provides a big challenge to a research scholar to read and summarize all the articles. Also, the researcher often finds difficult to identify and focus on the main area in the lengthy articles which is related to the current domain of the researcher. Hence, to overcome these issues, an architecture is proposed to integrate different NLP techniques to provide an abstract summary of a lengthy research paper. To provide a good quality to the abstract information, the methodology Reinforcement Learning is applied based on Human Feedback is used. The performance is validated through evaluation metrics. The outcome of the experimental study carried out proves it as an effective approach to process voluminous text, The proposed approach facilitates researchers, students, and professionals to quickly identifying key messages in the lengthy research publications

DOI:10.1109/ic366947.2025.11290129.abstract: Modern software development benefits greatly from automated code analysis tools that can detect bugs and suggest improvements. In this work, we present a transformer-based framework for code analysis that emphasizes both efficiency and interpretability. Our approach leverages pre-trained models to understand the syntax and semantics of the code and includes mechanisms to visualize the model’s attention for transparent error explanations. The system focuses on Python code, integrating pre-trained models like CodeBERT with modules for attention visualization, semantic analysis, and code parsing to address four key challenges: handling long code sequences via sparse attention mechanisms, mitigating biases in transformer predictions through adversarial training, incorporating code structure using Abstract Syntax Trees, and optimizing energy efficiency via model quantization and pruning. By prioritizing transparency through attention visualization and scalability through fragmentation strategies, this work provides a foundation for lightweight, developer-friendly code analysis tools. The results highlight the viability of transformer-based approaches for practical code optimization tasks while underscoring the need for continued research on energy-efficient model deployment and cross-language generalization.

DOI:10.1109/icassp49660.2025.10887724.abstract: Although MOTIP is the SOTA multi-object tracking method, there are still some issues that limit its performance. First, MOTIP still has defects in temporal information modeling, which leads to the failure to fully utilize the historical information of the tracked target and affects the correlation performance of the model. Second, in MOT, objects in consecutive video frames usually have temporal continuity and spatial consistency. Therefore, the object information of the previous frame can effectively assist the detection of the current frame. However, MOTIP performs independent detection between each frame, which does not fully utilize the correlation information between frames, resulting in suboptimal model performance. To address the above problems, we propose TrackFusion, which optimizes model performance from the perspective of trajectory modeling and inter-frame joint detection. First, we extract embeddings in video sequences through a Transformer-based detector, then combine the embeddings of the same object in different frames into sequences and input them into the trajectory modeling module for sequence association. This strategy effectively enhances the association ability. Thanks to these improvements, TrackFusion’s HOTA on the DanceTrack test set reached 68.6%, an increase of 1.1% compared to MOTIP’s 67.5%.

DOI:10.1109/icassp49660.2025.10889631.abstract: Social bot detection aims to precisely identify and mitigate the effects of bots spreading misinformation and manipulating public opinion by analyzing users’ textual content and network relationships on social media. Many existing methods rely on graph-based modalities, and while some incorporate multiple modalities, they often struggle to effectively capture the intricate interrelations within multimodal data. To address this limitation, we propose DMIBot, a dynamic multimodal interaction framework that comprehensively integrates metadata, text, and graph modalities. The framework utilizes a relational-aware graph aggregation module to enhance user node representations and a dynamic mixture of experts module to selectively engage the most appropriate expert for each sample. Furthermore, we introduce a synergistic interaction module that employs layer-wise recursive deep interaction mechanisms for efficient and effective integration of the three modalities. Experiments demonstrate that DMIBot outperforms nine benchmark models on two public datasets, achieving state-of-the-art performance in bot detection. Additional evaluations confirm its capabilities in ensuring the framework’s effectiveness and robustness in detecting Twitter bots.

DOI:10.1109/icbase70763.2026.11619398.abstract: Accurate skin lesion segmentation remains difficult because of low contrast and irregular boundaries. We present a reproducible enhancement to VM-UNet by integrating CBAM on skip features and ASPP at the bottleneck. Under a unified training pipeline, we evaluate baseline VM-UNet on ISIC17/ISIC18 and conduct controlled ablation on ISIC18. For the primary baseline versus CBAM+ASPP comparison, we run three seeds (42/43/44) and report mean±std. CBAM+ASPP improves mean overlap metrics over baseline on ISIC18 (mIoU $0.7960 \pm 0.0084$ vs. $\mathbf{0. 7 9 3 7} \pm \mathbf{0. 0 0 2 6}$, Dice $\mathbf{0. 8 8 6 4} \pm \mathbf{0. 0 0 5 2}$ vs. $\mathbf{0. 8 8 5 0} \pm \mathbf{0. 0 0 1 6}$) and reaches the best checkpoint with fewer epochs on average. These results indicate complementary effects of attention-guided feature refinement and multi-scale context aggregation in VM-UNet.

DOI:10.1109/iccc65529.2025.11148968.abstract: With the widespread adoption of Internet of Things (IoT) devices and the rapid advancement of edge computing technologies, there is a growing demand for the application of Large Language Models (LLMs) in IoT environments assisted by edge computing. However, unlike the batch processing inference mode of traditional artificial intelligence tasks, the inference process of large language models exhibits significant iterative characteristics. This results in the processing time of a single request not only depending on its task complexity but also being influenced by other requests within the same batch. Therefore, when designing scheduling strategies, it is essential to comprehensively consider the overall processing situation of each batch of tasks. Based on this, this study proposes an innovative finegrained scheduling method. This method first intelligently selects requests that need to be offloaded based on the real-time load status of computing nodes and network conditions. Secondly, by predicting the length of received requests, it dynamically adjusts the number of requests per batch to maximize the alignment of request processing times, thereby optimizing the overall system performance.

DOI:10.1109/icccas70754.2026.11672477.abstract: Post-placement congestion prediction is crucial for early routability analysis, yet accurate modeling remains challenging because layout congestion is sparse, spatially non-uniform, and even affected by long-range dependencies. Existing methods such as CircuitFormer model post-placement circuit components as point-based representations for grid-level prediction, but optimization on both their stability and bird’s-eye-view (BEV) feature refinement still remains open. To address this issue, we proposed CircuitFormer-Mamba, a hotspot-aware framework for post-placement congestion prediction. We first refined the CircuitFormer training recipe, which improves the validation Pearson coefficient from 0.5570 to 0.6488 and establishes a stronger baseline. Building upon this baseline, we incorporated a novel zero-init BEV Mamba Neck between the encoder and decoder to enhance long-range row-column contextual interactions while preserving the original prediction path through output-projection zero initialization. Experiments show that CircuitFormer-Mamba adds only 29,632 parameters, or 0.125% over the baseline, and achieves modest improvements in Pearson, Spearman, and Kendall coefficients on both the validation and test sets. On the test set, the three metrics increase by 0.34%, 2.23%, and 2.21%, respectively. As a result, the proposed framework improves the numerical hierarchy modeling of congestion hotspots, transition regions, and low-congestion areas, and forms a practical enhancement to CircuitFormer for post-placement congestion prediction.
